Technical details The root cause is a logic flaw (CWE-628: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments) combined with a prototype pollution gadget (CWE-1321). In lib/adapters/fetch.js, Axios builds a resolvedOptions object with sanitized headers and constructs a Request object from it, but then calls _fetch(request, fetchOptions) — passing the original, unsanitized fetchOptions as the second argument instead of resolvedOptions. In Node.js runtimes backed by undici, the second argument to fetch() can override headers already set on the Request object. If a separate prototype-pollution vulnerability in the same process has set Object.prototype.headers to attacker-controlled values, fetchOptions.headers resolves through prototype inheritance and overrides the sanitized headers. The fix in PR #11141 creates a null-prototype copy of fetchOptions (safeFetchOptions), strips Axios-managed fields (headers, method, body, signal, duplex, credentials) from it, and passes this safe copy as the second argument (GitHub Advisory, Fix Commit). Impact Successful exploitation allows an attacker to inject arbitrary HTTP headers — including Authorization, Cache-Control, and cloud metadata service access headers — into outbound requests made by the vulnerable Axios fetch adapter, while simultaneously suppressing legitimate caller-specified headers. This can lead to authorization bypass, cache poisoning, unauthorized access to cloud instance metadata services (e.g., AWS IMDSv1), or manipulation of application-specific header-based security controls. The vulnerability does not affect confidentiality or availability of the vulnerable system directly, but poses a high integrity risk to subsequent systems receiving the manipulated requests (GitHub Advisory, Feedly).
